summary: All 65 rules opened in my own downloads of the primary sources (eCFR API current to 2026-11-19, apps.legislature.ky.gov statutes and KAR, the official 2026 Indiana Code title files that iga.in.gov loads, LII U.S. Code, CMS, OIG, GovInfo court opinions, and the payers' own documents). Every researcher quote was found verbatim. 58 correct (many with notes that add limits or stronger text), 7 corrected (TR-21 transparency files move to quarterly per-network files from March 6, 2027; TR-24 'fraud or similar fault' and the unappealable, dismissible clerical reopening; TR-46 Barrows dismissed North Carolina statutes, mostly by concession; TR-47 the PxDx sentence quoted was the complaint, not the holding; TR-48 missing Class A misdemeanor tier and 90-day aggregation; TR-49 now read in the official code, clause is (c)(1)(F) and threats tied to a person's occupation are a Level 6 felony; TR-55 the 180-day period suspends the 60-day clock, it is not the deadline). None wrong; none could not be checked, though TR-50's current court text was confirmed only through the bar's reproduction (kycourts.gov returned 403).

checks.citation: 42 CFR 422.568(c), (d)(1), (e)(2), (f); 42 CFR 422.566(a) for the applicable integrated plan carve-out
checks.quote: (2) State the specific reasons for the denial; ... If the MA organization fails to provide the enrollee and the physician or provider involved, as appropriate, with timely notice of an organization determination as specified in this section, this failure itself constitutes an adverse organization determination and may be appealed.
checks.correction: Note: the payment clock comes from 422.568(c): 'The MA organization must process requests for payment according to the "prompt payment" provisions set forth in § 422.520.' The integrated-plan exclusion is in 422.566(a), not 422.568. Read in the eCFR (API, data current to 2026-11-19).

checks.citation: 42 CFR 422.566(d); 42 CFR 422.566(b)(3); CMS FAQ of Feb. 6, 2024, Question 9
checks.quote: the organization determination must be reviewed by a physician or other appropriate health care professional with expertise in the field of medicine or health care that is appropriate for the services at issue, including knowledge of Medicare coverage criteria, before the MA organization issues the organization determination decision. The physician or health care professional reviewing the request need not, in all cases, be of the same specialty or subspecialty as the treating physician
checks.correction: Note: FAQ Q9 confirmed ('the refusal to provide or pay for services, in whole or in part ... is an organization determination by the MA plan under § 422.566(b)(3)'). The reviewer must also hold a current and unrestricted license. At reconsideration the bar is higher: 42 CFR 422.590(h)(2) requires the reconsidered medical-necessity decision to be made 'by a physician with expertise in the field of medicine that is appropriate for the services at issue', and 422.590(h)(1) by someone 'not involved in making the organization determination'.

checks.quote: MA organizations may create publicly accessible internal coverage criteria that are based on current evidence in widely used treatment guidelines or clinical literature when coverage criteria are not fully established in applicable Medicare statutes, regulations, NCDs or LCDs. ... (A) The internal coverage criteria in use and a summary of evidence that was considered during the development of the internal coverage criteria used to make medical necessity determinations;
checks.correction: Note: the operative bar is (c)(1)(i)(A): MA organizations 'may not deny coverage for basic benefits based on coverage criteria not specified in paragraph (b) or (c) of this section.' (b)(6)(ii)(B)-(C) also require the list of evidence sources and the rationale to be public.

checks.citation: CMS HPMS memo to all MA organizations and Medicare-Medicaid Plans, 'Frequently Asked Questions related to Coverage Criteria and Utilization Management Requirements in CMS Final Rule (CMS-4201-F)', Feb. 6, 2024, Question 2 (interpreting 42 CFR 422.101(c))
checks.quote: an algorithm that determines coverage based on a larger data set instead of the individual patient's medical history, the physician's recommendations, or clinical notes would not be compliant with § 422.101(c). ... Because publicly posted coverage criteria are static and unchanging, artificial intelligence cannot be used to shift the coverage criteria over time.
checks.correction: Note: guidance, not regulation. Pair it with the binding text, 42 CFR 422.101(c)(1)(i)(C): decisions must be based on 'The enrollee's medical history (for example, diagnoses, conditions, functional status), physician recommendations, and clinical notes.' No AI-specific regulatory text was found in 42 CFR 422.101, 422.112 or 422.137 in the eCFR current to 2026-11-19.

checks.quote: If the MA organization affirms, in whole or in part, its adverse organization determination, it must prepare a written explanation and send the case file to the independent entity contracted by CMS no later than 60 calendar days from the date it receives the request for a standard reconsideration. ... this failure constitutes an affirmation of its adverse organization determination, and the MA organization must submit the file to the independent entity
checks.correction: Note: a non-contract provider is a party only as 'an assignee of the enrollee (that is, a physician or other provider who has furnished a service to the enrollee and formally agrees to waive any right to payment from the enrollee for that service)' (422.574(b)). The practice's own filing clock is 422.582(b): 'within 60 calendar days after receipt of the written organization determination notice.' The IRE status lookup named in CMS's 2027 Star Ratings technical notes is https://partcappeals.c2cinc.com/Search-Appeal-Status.

checks.citation: CMS 2027 Star Ratings Technical Notes (last updated 11/04/2026), Part C Measure C31 Reviewing Appeals Decisions (p. 85)
checks.quote: This rating shows how often an independent reviewer found the health plan's decision to deny coverage to be reasonable. ... This includes appeals requested by a beneficiary, appeals requested by a party on behalf of a beneficiary, and appeals requested by non-contract providers.
checks.correction: Note: Weighting Value 2 confirmed. Cut points: 5 stars only at 100% upheld, 4 stars at 98% to under 100%, 1 star under 88%. Only IRE (level 2) decisions count; dismissed and withdrawn appeals are excluded; 10 or fewer appeals means not enough data. The 2027 ratings use CY2025 appeals.

checks.citation: 42 CFR 422.125(a), (b)(3), (c); CMS 2027 Star Ratings Technical Notes, Measure C27 Complaints about the Health Plan

checks.correction: Note: the Complaints Tracking Module records complaints 'from beneficiaries and others' (422.125(a)). Measure C27 counts all CTM complaints per 1,000 members (some subcategories excluded by CMS's CTM procedures). I did not verify a CMS online provider complaint form; that point rests on the medicare_advantage area.

checks.correction: Note: (h)(3)(ii) adds that the appeal must 'not afford deference to the initial adverse benefit determination' and be decided by someone who is neither the original decision-maker nor that person's subordinate; (h)(3)(v) bars reusing the professional consulted on the initial denial.

checks.quote: In the case of a plan or issuer that fails to strictly adhere to all the requirements of this paragraph (b)(2) with respect to a claim, the claimant is deemed to have exhausted the internal claims and appeals process of this paragraph (b) ... checks.correction: Note: (F)(2) also gives a 10-day right to a written explanation of any violation, a cheap second lever. Federal external review under (d)(1)(i)(A) covers determinations that involve medical judgment (and a few listed categories), so deemed exhaustion on a pure pricing dispute leads to court, not external review. Non-grandfathered plans only.

The title of the reviewer making the decision, except that a written notice provided to a provider shall also include, if applicable, the medical license number of the reviewer making the decision; ... failure to make a determination and provide written notice within the time frames set forth in this section shall be deemed to be a prior authorization for the health care services or benefits subject to the review.
checks.correction: Note: Medicaid MCO coverage confirmed (KRS 205.522(1)(m) lists 'KRS 304.17A-600, 304.17A-603, and 304.17A-607'). Deemed authorization does not apply where the delay 'results from circumstances which are documented to be beyond the insurer's control' ((3)(b)). Related and stronger for appeals: KRS 304.17A-617(4)(b) and (4)(d)2 (see missing).

checks.quote: adverse determinations based on medical necessity are made; and (B) appeals are reviewed and decided; by a clinical peer ... is certified in the same specialty as the physician under review ... owes a duty to the covered individual to exercise the applicable standard of care. ... the health care service subject to prior authorization shall be automatically deemed authorized by the utilization review entity.
checks.correction: Note: 'adverse determination' (27-1-37.5-1.5) covers a service 'furnished or proposed to be furnished', so the clinical-peer rule in -20 reaches retrospective medical-necessity denials made by an entity that performs prior authorization (-8.3); the automatic authorization in -28 is limited to services subject to prior authorization. A clinical peer may not decide an appeal if involved in the denial or financially interested (-20(b)). Read from the official 2026 Title 27 file that the iga.in.gov viewer loads.

An insurer may not alter the CPT code submitted for a clean claim or pay for a CPT code of lesser monetary value unless: (1) the CPT code submitted is not in accordance with correct coding guidelines and rules, clinical care guidelines, or the terms and conditions of the participating provider's agreement or contract with the insurer; or (2) the medical record of the clean claim has been reviewed by an employee or contractor of the insurer.

checks.correction: Note: the same section has stronger provider tools the area did not list: (1)(c) reprocessing without rebilling, (1)(d) appeal and payment clocks, (1)(e) audit and recoupment limits (see missing).

checks.quote: A provider may submit multiple claims to be appealed in a single external independent third-party review if the provider alleges that a Medicaid managed care organization has implemented a policy or practice that results in the denial, in whole or in part, of those claims. ... Any claim that remains unpaid for forty-five (45) days or more after the date the claim is received by the managed care organization and that individually or in the aggregate exceeds two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500);
checks.correction: Caution: 907 KAR 17:035 (last amended effective 5-4-2018, before the statute's current text) still says in Section 3(3) 'Only one (1) claim shall be reviewed per external independent third-party review unless the department determines that reviewing multiple claims related to one (1) member is expedient and appropriate.' The statute applies 'Notwithstanding any law to the contrary', so cite KRS 205.646(2) when an MCO or the Department invokes the regulation. 60-day filing deadline confirmed (907 KAR 17:035 Section 2(1)(a)). The hearing fee is up to $1,000, one fee for a bundled hearing, paid by the losing party (KRS 205.646(6)); either side may appeal the reviewer's decision within 30 days (205.646(4)).

checks.quote: (i) The in-network rate and out-of-network allowed amount machine-readable files required by paragraphs (b)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section must be updated and posted quarterly on the first day of each calendar-year quarter beginning with the first calendar-year quarter following the applicability date under paragraph (c)(1) of this section; ... The provisions of this section apply beginning March 6, 2027, except that paragraphs (b)(2), (b)(3)(iii), and (b)(4)(iii) through (v) of this section apply beginning September 6, 2027.
checks.correction: The researcher's quotes match the text in force on 2026-11-23, but 'monthly' files are ending. The Oct. 6, 2026 final rule (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-06/pdf/2026-20447.pdf, effective Dec. 7, 2026) restructures the in-network rate file per provider network and moves it to quarterly posting from March 6, 2027; until then plans must keep complying with the July 1, 2025 text. Rates stay associated with NPI, TIN and place of service. RemitWatch should plan for quarterly files in 2027 and cite the file date it priced against.

checks.citation: KRS 304.17A-708(2), (3)(a)-(b); applies to Kentucky Medicaid MCOs through KRS 205.593(2)
checks.quote: An insurer shall not be required to correct a payment error to a provider if the provider's request for a payment correction is filed more than twenty-four (24) months after the date that the provider received payment for the claim from the insurer. ... Except in cases of fraud, an insurer may only retroactively deny reimbursement to a provider during the twenty-four (24) month period after the date that the insurer paid the claim submitted by the provider.
checks.correction: Note: a retroactive denial must come with 'a written or electronic statement specifying the basis for the retroactive denial' ((3)(b)). Overpayment recoupment has its own 24-month notice and dispute rules in KRS 304.17A-714 (see missing).

checks.citation: IC 27-8-5.7-10(a)-(f) as amended by P.L.88-2026 SECTION 10 (effective July 1, 2026); IC 27-8-5.7-0.5; HMO counterpart IC 27-13-36.2-8 and 27-13-36.2-0.5
checks.quote: An insurer may not recoup a paid claim more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the date on which the claim was initially paid. ... An insurer may not retroactively audit a paid claim more than three (3) years after the date on which the claim was initially paid. ... An insurer may not be required to correct a payment error to a provider if notice of the payment error is not provided within one hundred eighty (180) days after payment for a fully adjudicated claim is received.
checks.correction: Note: the 2025 text did allow two years each way (checked in https://iga.in.gov/ic/2025/Title_27.html). HMOs have the same 180-day, 3-year and 180-day limits in IC 27-13-36.2-8, for contracts 'entered into, delivered, amended, or renewed after June 30, 2026' covering plan years after Dec. 31, 2026 (27-13-36.2-0.5).

checks.quote: At any time if there exists reliable evidence as defined in § 405.902 that the initial determination was procured by fraud or similar fault as defined in § 405.902. ... A party may request that a contractor reopen its initial determination at any time if the initial determination is unfavorable, in whole or in part, to the party thereto, but only for the purpose of correcting a clerical error on which that determination was based. Third party payer error does not constitute clerical error. ... The contractor's, QIC's, ALJ's or attorney adjudicator's, or Council's decision on whether to reopen is binding and not subject to appeal.
checks.correction: The any-time exception is 'fraud or similar fault', not fraud alone, so old payments are not safe whenever 'similar fault' could be shown. Clerical-error reopenings have real limits the area left out: if the contractor 'disagrees that the issue is a clerical error, the contractor must dismiss the reopening request' and gives appeal rights only if the original appeal window is still open ((a)(3)); the decision whether to reopen is not appealable ((a)(5)); no reopening while the claim is under appeal ((a)(4)). File clerical reopenings while the redetermination window is still open when possible ('within 120 calendar days from the date a party receives the notice of the initial determination', 42 CFR 405.942(a)).

checks.quote: An insurer shall not require a provider to appeal errors in payment where the insurer has not paid the claim according to the contracted rate. Miscalculations in payments made by the insurer shall be corrected and paid within thirty (30) calendar days upon the insurer's receipt of documentation from the provider verifying the error. ... An insurer shall not be required to pay interest on corrected payments made in accordance with KRS 304.17A-708(1).
checks.correction: Note: KRS 304.12-230(17) confirmed: 'Knowingly and willfully failing to comply with the provisions of KRS 304.17A-708 on resolution of payment errors and retroactive denial of claims.' 806 KAR 17:360 read at https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/806/017/360/.

checks.quote: the insurer shall add the interest payable to the amount of the unpaid claim without the necessity for any claim for that interest to be made by the provider filing the original claim. ... shall pay the interest required by KRS 304.17A-730 within thirty (30) days after the date a claim is paid.
checks.correction: Note: rates confirmed (12% for 1-30 days late, 18% for 31-60, 21% over 60, per annum, from the date payment was due under 304.17A-702, which is 30 calendar days from receipt). Interest does not apply where the delay results from 'acts or events beyond the control of the insurer' (730(2)). 806 KAR 17:360 Section 4(2) requires each interest payment to identify the claim, so missing interest is detectable on the 835.

checks.quote: If an insurer fails to settle a claim within the time prescribed in subsection (1) of this section and the delay was without reasonable foundation, the insured person or health care provider shall be entitled to be reimbursed for his reasonable attorney's fees incurred.

A fine of one thousand dollars ($1,000) per day or ten percent (10%) of the unpaid claim amount, whichever is greater, for each day that a clean claim remains unpaid ... has a pattern of repeated violations of KRS 304.17A-700 to 304.17A-730
checks.correction: Note: the compliance safe harbor in (2) is measured per calendar quarter (95% of clean claims adjudicated on time and 90% of clean-claim dollars paid on time); (3) extends the fines to Medicaid MCOs.

checks.correction: Note: 'Written communications' include 'all correspondence, regardless of source or type' (Section 1(16)), so a provider's letter counts. Section 3(9) adds: written notice of denial 'within fifteen (15) calendar days of the determination' that refers to the policy provision relied on. Regulation read at https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/806/012/092/.

checks.quote: The internal appeals process may be initiated by the covered person, an authorized person, or a provider acting on behalf of the covered person. ... A covered person, an authorized person, or a provider acting on behalf of and with the consent of the covered person, may request an external review of an adverse benefit determination, other than a coverage denial, rendered by an insurer, its designee, or agent.
checks.correction: Note: external review also requires that 'The entire course of treatment or service will cost the covered person at least one hundred dollars ($100) if the covered person had no insurance' ((3)(d)); the request is due within 60 days of the internal appeal decision with written consent for records ((4)); the covered person pays a $25 fee, refundable and waivable ((5)). Confirmed in KRS 304.17A-625 (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57347): 'The insurer shall be responsible for the cost of the external review' ((5)); the decision 'shall be binding on the insurer with respect to that covered person' ((9)(a)); refusal to comply requires the insurer 'to pay the claim that was the subject of the external review, without need for the covered person or authorized person to further establish a right as to the payment amount' and makes it bear reasonable attorney's fees ((10)). KRS 304.17A-617 read at https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57343.

checks.correction: The rule is not 'within 180 days while an investigation runs'. A timely, good-faith investigation suspends the 60-day deadline until the earlier of its completion or day 180; after that the remainder of the 60 days runs (CMS's example: investigation started on day 10 leaves 50 days after the suspension ends), so the outside date is about 240 days. The last quoted sentence is CMS's preamble, 89 FR 98337-98338 (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-12-09/html/2024-25382.htm). 'Identified' means the person 'knowingly receives or retains an overpayment' under the False Claims Act's knowledge standard (401.305(a)(2)). Lookback 6 years and False Claims Act 'obligation' confirmed. 401.305 is the Medicare Parts A and B rule; the statute names MA organizations and Medicaid MCOs as 'persons', but whether provider payments from an MA plan are 'funds ... under subchapter XVIII' stays unconfirmed.

missing: 42 CFR 422.138(c) (eCFR, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-422.138): an MA prior authorization locks the medical-necessity question. 'If the MA organization approved the furnishing of a covered item or service through a prior authorization or pre-service determination of coverage or payment ... it may not deny coverage later on the basis of lack of medical necessity and may not reopen such a decision for any reason except for good cause ... or if there is reliable evidence of fraud or similar fault'. Directly useful for authorized Mohs and radiation; CMS FAQ Q9 (Feb. 6, 2024) says post-claim audits must respect it.

42 CFR 422.590(h)(1)-(2) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-422.590): an MA reconsideration must be done by 'A person or persons who were not involved in making the organization determination', and a medical-necessity reconsideration 'must be made by a physician with expertise in the field of medicine that is appropriate for the services at issue' (same specialty not required in all cases). Stronger than 422.566(d) at the appeal stage.

42 CFR 422.562(a)(4) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-422.562): every MA organization 'must employ a medical director who is responsible for ensuring the clinical accuracy of all organization determinations and reconsiderations involving medical necessity'. A named target when asking who answers for an automated denial.

42 CFR 422.101(c)(1)(i)(A), (C) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-422.101): the binding rule behind the CMS AI FAQ. MA plans 'may not deny coverage for basic benefits based on coverage criteria not specified in paragraph (b) or (c)' and must base medical-necessity decisions on 'The enrollee's medical history (for example, diagnoses, conditions, functional status), physician recommendations, and clinical notes.'

42 CFR 422.582(b) and 422.574(b) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-422.582): the practice's own MA clock and standing. A reconsideration 'must be filed within 60 calendar days after receipt of the written organization determination notice'; a non-contract provider is a party as 'an assignee of the enrollee (that is, a physician or other provider who has furnished a service to the enrollee and formally agrees to waive any right to payment from the enrollee for that service)'.

42 CFR 422.510(a)(4)(ii) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-422.510): CMS may terminate an MA contract where the organization 'Substantially failed to comply with the requirements in subpart M of this part relating to grievances and appeals' (alongside (a)(4)(v), prompt payment). Gives a pattern complaint about ignored appeals regulatory weight.

29 CFR 2560.503-1(c)(2) and (h)(3)(ii) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-2560.503-1): a group health plan may not require 'more than two appeals of an adverse benefit determination prior to bringing a civil action', and the appeal must 'not afford deference to the initial adverse benefit determination' and be decided by someone who is neither the original decision-maker nor that person's subordinate.

KRS 304.17A-617(4)(a)-(b), (4)(d)2, (5) (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57343, effective July 15, 2026): Kentucky internal appeals must be decided 'Within thirty (30) days of receipt of the request'; an appeal of an adverse determination other than a coverage denial 'shall only be conducted by a licensed physician who did not participate in the initial review and denial', and on request by the provider the insurer 'shall ... utilize a board-eligible or certified physician in the appropriate specialty or subspecialty area'; the appeal decision letter to a provider must include 'the medical license number of the person making the decision'. Coverage denials can go to the Department, which calls for the insurer's response 'within ten (10) business days' ((5)(c)). Applies to Medicaid MCOs only where KRS 205.522 lists it (it lists 304.17A-600, -603 and -607, not -617).

KRS 205.534(1)(c)-(e), (6) (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57033): Kentucky Medicaid MCOs must 'Reprocess claims that are incorrectly paid or denied in error, in compliance with KRS 304.17A-708. The reprocessing shall not require a provider to rebill or resubmit claims to obtain correct payment. A claim shall not be denied for timely filing if the initial claim was timely submitted'; must accept provider appeals filed 'within one hundred twenty (120) days of confirmed receipt' of the reduction or denial and decide them 'within thirty (30) days' (failure subject to contract fines under (6)); must pay within 30 days after a favorable appeal; and in audits must allow 30 days for records, finish within 180 days, and 'Only recoup denied payments or issue a demand for payment from a provider upon the final disposition of the audit, including the appeals process established in KRS 205.646'.

KRS 304.17A-714(1)-(4) (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=29336): the defense against Kentucky takebacks. Except for rate or method errors, an insurer must give overpayment notice 'within twenty-four (24) months from the date that the insurer paid the claim' with 'the basis for determining that an overpayment exists'; a provider dispute filed within 30 days means 'no recoupment shall be made until the dispute is resolved', and disputes must be 'completed within thirty (30) days'. Knowing and willful violation is an unfair claims settlement practice (KRS 304.12-230(16)).

907 KAR 17:035 Sections 2(1)(a), 3(3), 5 (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/907/017/035/): request Kentucky Medicaid external review 'within sixty (60) calendar days of receiving the MCO's final decision'; the 2018 regulation still says 'Only one (1) claim shall be reviewed per external independent third-party review' unless the Department finds multiple claims for one member expedient, which conflicts with the bundling right in KRS 205.646(2) and should be met by citing the statute; and 'Within sixty (60) calendar days from the exhaustion of appeal rights after a final decision against an MCO ... the MCO shall submit complete payment as required by the decision.'

806 KAR 12:092 Section 3(9) (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/806/012/092/): 'When a claim is denied, written notice of denial shall be sent to the claimant within fifteen (15) calendar days of the determination. The notice shall refer to the policy provision, condition, or exclusion upon which the denial is based.' A bare remark code is not that notice (guidance for the commissioner, Section 2(2)).

IC 27-1-52-8 and 27-1-52-13 (https://iga.in.gov/ic/2026/Title_27.html, effective July 1, 2026): an Indiana insurer 'may not use downcoding in a manner that prevents a provider from: (1) submitting a health benefits claim for the actual health care service performed; and (2) collecting reimbursement from the insurer for the actual health care service performed', and 'may not downcode in a targeted or discriminatory manner against providers that routinely treat patients with complex or chronic conditions.' Not Medicaid (27-1-52-0.3).

IC 27-8-5.7-6.7 and IC 27-13-36.2-4.7 (https://iga.in.gov/ic/2026/Title_27.html, P.L.88-2026): Indiana insurers and HMOs 'may not retroactively reduce the reimbursement rate for any CPT code' and must give 'at least sixty (60) days' notice by mail or email and website posting before a prospective rate cut; applies to policies and HMO contracts issued, delivered, amended or renewed after June 30, 2026 that cover plan years beginning after Dec. 31, 2026 (27-8-5.7-0.5; 27-13-36.2-0.5). A ready check for unannounced fee-schedule drops.

IC 27-13-15-1(d) (https://iga.in.gov/ic/2026/Title_27.html): an Indiana HMO 'must provide the participating provider with a current reimbursement rate schedule: (1) every two (2) years; and (2) when three (3) or more CPT code ... rates under the contract change in a twelve (12) month period.' A lawful demand that supplies the rate evidence for underpayment proof.

IC 27-8-5.7-11.5 (https://iga.in.gov/ic/2026/Title_27.html, P.L.88-2026): after an Indiana insurer or HMO 'recoups payment from a provider due to an error in coordination of benefits', the provider may bill the right insurer 'not later than ninety (90) days after the date the recoupment is made', with proof of the original submission and the recoupment. A clock RemitWatch should run on every COB takeback.

IC 33-29-2-4(b)(1); IC 33-28-3-4(b)(1) (https://iga.in.gov/ic/2026/Title_33.html): Indiana small claims dockets hear civil actions where 'the amount sought or value of the property sought to be recovered is not more than ten thousand dollars ($10,000)' (after June 30, 2021); answers the area's open question and is four times Kentucky's $2,500 limit.

42 CFR 438.406(b)(2)(i), (b)(5) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-438.406): Medicaid managed care appeals must be decided by individuals 'neither involved in any previous level of review or decision-making nor a subordinate of any such individual', and the plan must give the enrollee and representative the case file, 'including medical records, other documents and records, and any new or additional evidence considered, relied upon, or generated', 'free of charge and sufficiently in advance of the resolution timeframe'.
